name: GridPatch Night Maintenance Street-to-Site Rig
description: Infrastructure maintenance workers who pull night shifts on Circuit's open-air conduit grid — fixing cracked pipes, patching acid-rain erosion on overpass supports, splicing power lines at two in the morning — wear a rig that has to take them from the transit stop to the job site and back without standing out as a target. The outer shell is a hooded work jacket in slate grey synth-canvas, mid-thigh length with a drawstring hem, raglan sleeves cut wide enough to accommodate a full chrome arm prosthetic with room for a tool strap underneath. Subtle reflective piping runs along the hood edge and cuffs — visible to vehicles but not obvious from a distance. The jacket back carries a large embroidered patch: the GridPatch municipal maintenance logo, a stylized circuit-board hexagon in faded yellow-orange on grey. Underneath is a heavyweight navy henley in thermal synth-cotton, long-sleeved with reinforced elbow patches in darker navy canvas. The trousers are Fenmark ToughSeam-style in charcoal, with articulated knees, a waterproof coating on the lower legs and seat, and six pockets including two large cargo pockets on the thigh sealed with hook-and-bar closures. A tool belt in worn black leather-analog sits over the waistband — spanner loops, a multi-tool holster, and a small lamp clip. Boots are mid-cut waterproof work boots with a composite toe and deep lug sole for wet grating and scaffold work. A knit neck gaiter in charcoal doubles as a face cover in acid-drizzle conditions, and a battered hard-foam bump cap with a built-in LED strip completes the head.
functionality: Acid-rain and moisture resistance on lower garments, wide raglan sleeves for chrome arm accommodation, tool belt integration, LED bump cap for hands-free worksite lighting, neck gaiter for chemical drizzle protection, subtle reflective trim for vehicle visibility, waterproof lower trouser panels for standing water and grating work
what_it_says: Municipal worker. Not glamorous, not corporate — GridPatch is a city-contracted outfit that pays steadily but slowly. The faded patch says they've had this jacket a while. The tool belt is personal — not issued — and the wear on the leather shows which tools they reach for most. They move through the city at night like they own it, because they kind of do.
manufacturer: GridPatch Municipal Maintenance Division (jacket and trousers); tool belt self-assembled from market hardware
price_range: Φ160–Φ240 full rig (jacket Φ90, trousers Φ70, boots Φ80 separate)
story_hooks: A GridPatch crew member discovers a sealed access panel on a routine conduit run that isn't on any city infrastructure map — behind it is a hardwired data tap that's been pulling live transit and surveillance feeds for an unknown duration.

Someone in this rig has been seen at three separate crime scenes in the last month — always as a background figure in footage, always appearing to work, never flagged because maintenance workers are invisible on Circuit streets at night.

The GridPatch embroidered patch on the jacket back has been quietly redesigned — the new version contains a microscopic RFID tag that logs worker location every fifteen minutes; the old-patch crew are the only ones who haven't been updated yet.

physical_description.visual_profile: Utilitarian night-shift worker silhouette — practical, low-profile, designed for mobility and durability. Slate grey jacket with faded yellow-orange municipal patch creates a deliberately unremarkable appearance suitable for navigating industrial infrastructure zones after dark. The wide raglan sleeves and articulated knees telegraph functional augmentation accommodation rather than style.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed but tailored for movement — jacket mid-thigh with drawstring hem for adjustability, raglan sleeves wide enough to clear cybernetic limbs, articulated knee panels for climbing and crouching. All proportions favor access and tool-carrying capacity over silhouette.
physical_description.primary_material: Slate grey synth-canvas jacket (waterproof, acid-resistant), navy thermal synth-cotton henley, charcoal ToughSeam articulated trousers with waterproof polymer coating on lower legs and seat, worn black leather-analog tool belt
physical_description.texture: Canvas has a slightly weathered matte finish; henley is soft-knit with reinforced canvas elbow patches showing faint fraying; trousers have a technical ripstop weave with subtle articulation stitching at knees; tool belt shows genuine creasing and patina from repeated use
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: slate grey and charcoal with navy accents. Secondary: faded yellow-orange embroidered municipal patch (circuit-board hexagon). Reflective piping in pale silver along hood edge and cuffs — subtle but visible to vehicle sensors.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: drawstring hood and hem, raglan sleeve adjustment points. Henley: standard buttons. Trousers: standard waistband closure plus six pockets sealed with hook-and-bar (cargo pockets), allowing quick access without fumbling. Tool belt: traditional leather loops and magnetic snaps.
distinctive_features: Large embroidered GridPatch municipal maintenance patch on jacket back — circuit-board hexagon in faded yellow-orange
Reflective piping along hood edge and cuffs for vehicle visibility without aesthetic compromise
Reinforced navy canvas elbow patches on henley showing wear patterns from scaffolding work
Articulated knee panels on trousers with reinforced stitching
Waterproof polymer coating on lower legs and seat (visible as slight sheen)
Wide raglan sleeves engineered to accommodate full chrome prosthetics with underarm tool strap routing
Worn black leather-analog tool belt with spanner loops, multi-tool holster, and lamp clip
Hook-and-bar sealed cargo pockets (practical for wet environments and quick access)
Hard-foam bump cap with integrated LED strip headlamp
Charcoal knit neck gaiter (functions as acid-drizzle face protection)
Composite-toe mid-cut waterproof work boots with deep lug sole
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional — working-class infrastructure maintenance. Quality is genuine and built to last; the outfit signals competence and grid-system authorization rather than wealth.
physical_description.cultural_context: Municipal infrastructure worker on permanent night shift. This outfit signals legitimacy in industrial zones and conduit access areas — the GridPatch patch is functional security clearance made visible. The wearer is invisible to the city during daylight but essential after dark. Suggests someone comfortable with augmentation, chemical/environmental hazards, and solo fieldwork.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and well-maintained but not pristine. The jacket patch fades naturally from UV and acid spray; elbows show gentle fraying; tool belt leather has creases and polish marks from repeated use. The overall impression is 'this person actually works,' not parade-ready.
